name: Kottakkal Arya Vaidya Sala
tagline: Kerala’s century-old centre for classical Ayurveda and herbal medicines
summary: Founded in 1902 at Kottakkal, Arya Vaidya Sala (AVS) is a world‑renowned charitable Ayurvedic hospital, medicine manufacturer, research and education centre offering classical treatments and…
description: Kottakkal Arya Vaidya Sala (AVS) is an Ayurvedic charitable institution and hospital founded by Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier in 1902 at Kottakkal, Malappuram. It combines classical patient care, an in‑house pharmacy, research and an education (pathashala) tradition.

AVS matters because it helped revive authentic Kerala Ayurveda on a large scale: it runs the charitable hospital and outpatient services, manufactures classical Ayurvedic medicines, supports training and publishes research and texts rooted in the traditional gurusukula system.

Visitors come for clinical consultations, panchakarma and specialist clinics, to buy trusted Kottakkal medicines, to visit the small museum/herbal garden and to see the campus that shaped Kottakkal’s reputation as an Ayurveda town.
AVS balances tradition and modern quality controls: in recent years it has expanded services and testing capability while keeping classical treatment principles at the core.
highlights: Charitable hospital and specialist outpatient clinics
Classical panchakarma treatments and physician consultations
In‑house manufacturing of classical Ayurvedic medicines
Herbal garden and small museum on the Kottakkal campus
Centre for training (Aryavaidya Patasala / VPSV) and research

sections.heading: Background
body: Arya Vaidya Sala was established in 1902 by Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier as a village clinic that grew into an internationally recognised Ayurvedic institution. Over the decades AVS added a teaching pathashala, a charitable hospital, manufacturing units and branch clinics across India.

The institution preserves classical texts and therapies while developing quality control and research capacities; it continues to be run as a charitable trust and remains central to Kottakkal’s identity as an Ayurveda hub.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Consult with an AVS physician (book ahead). The campus offers outpatient clinics, inpatient panchakarma programmes at its Ayurvedic Hospital & Research Centre, and specialty OP services announced periodically.

Browse the pharmacy for authentic AVS formulations, visit the herb garden and the small museum/archive that illustrate the history of P.S. Varier and the institution’s role in propagating Kerala Ayurveda.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Book consultations and panchakarma packages directly with AVS before you travel; the hospital runs scheduled programmes and some specialty clinics may require advance appointments.

Bring prior medical records and a clear list of medications and allergies. Respect clinic guidance for diet and treatment schedules; ask AVS staff about stays in the inpatient ward versus outpatient therapies.

latest.text: CRISIL re‑affirmed credit ratings for Arya Vaidya Sala, Kottakkal (rating factsheet published September 9, 2026).
AVS launched two new consumer products — Brahmi Plus and Dige Plus Gummies — announced in May 2026.
AVS announced 'Trinaya', its first franchise wellness centre (press announcement for Trinaya Banjara Hills, Hyderabad).
AVS upgraded its quality‑control lab with a modern spectroscopy instrument (ICP‑OES) to test raw materials and finished medicines.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November–February for sightseeing; consult AVS about the best months for panchakarma (many therapies are scheduled year‑round).
visitorInfo.howToReach: Kottakkal lies on NH66 in Malappuram district. Nearest airport: Calicut (Kozhikode) International Airport, approximately 25 km. Nearest major railway station: Tirur (about 14 km). From those hubs take road transport to Kottakkal and the AVS campus (confirm local connections before travel).
etiquette: Book doctor consultations and any panchakarma packages well in advance, especially during festival and peak tourist seasons.
Bring medical records and a list of current medicines; follow the clinic’s dietary and treatment instructions strictly.
Respect local customs on the campus (modest clothing) and permit time for therapies which may span several days.
Confirm treatment inclusions, tariffs and stay arrangements with AVS directly before you travel.
